title: Treasury International Capital (TIC) monthly release (November 2026 data) — the first annual-revision edition of 2027, 4:00 p.m. ET
source: EST: home.treasury.gov/data/treasury-international-capital-tic-system/release-dates-of-tic-data, fetched direct 2026-09-08 (plain curl, HTTP 200) by the tic-monthly-2026-11-18 initial-research adjacency sweep — its 2027 table's January row reads '19' in the Monthly column, under the page header 'All data releases occur at 4 p.m. Washington, D.C. time', with the Quarterly and Annual columns empty. Reference month November 2026 by the page's own 1.5-month lag rule. Corroborated mechanically and EXACTLY: with federal holidays excluded (New Year's Day 2027-01-01, MLK 2027-01-18) the 11th business day of January 2027 is 2027-01-19, offset +0 on the page's published '11th business day plus 0 to 3 days' rule — the same holiday-aware convention that reproduces 22 of the 24 published 2026-27 dates and hits 9 exactly, recomputed from scratch by this session rather than inherited. Filed estimate per this lane's no-self-confirm limit on an event discovered in-sweep: the proposer may not confirm what it found, only the event's own session may. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: DISCOVERED during the tic-monthly-2026-11-18 initial research (2026-09-08) from that event's own primary fetch of Treasury's release-dates page. Proposed for two reasons that are specific rather than serial. (1) IT IS THE NEXT UNCLAIMED SLOT: 2026-12-15 already exists as `proposals/tic-monthly-2026-12-15.from-tic-monthly-2026-10-16.json`, and a second proposal for the same id would be a competing proposal the validator warns on — so this sweep proposes the first slot nobody owns rather than duplicating one. (2) IT IS A REVISION EDITION, and the revision/non-revision split is now the only cut that separates TIC releases at all. Treasury's own note (c) makes January one of the four releases that 'reflect revised data for the past year', so it restates the twelve months every valuation model on this calendar is fitted on — including the two months (August 2026, September 2026) whose forward tests tic-monthly-2026-10-16 and tic-monthly-2026-11-18 register. A revision edition can move the very observations those tests were scored against, which is a scheduling fact worth having on the calendar with lead time rather than at D-3. It also sits the session AFTER the MLK closure (2027-01-18) and two sessions before vix-expiration-2027-01-20, inside the fomc-blackout-start-2027-01-16 window ahead of fomc-2027-01-27. Impact LOW and symbols empty on the standing grounds (16:00 ET is after the equity cash close, the data is six weeks stale, no house playbook is macro-keyed). Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
